evaluations.question: Tell me about a time you had to design or operate a high-throughput transaction system where duplicate execution or data drift could cause severe financial loss.
evaluations.candidate_response: In ERP and fintech procurement, ledger drift and duplicate payments cost millions. To solve this, I architected ApexFlow, a high-throughput 3-way reconciliation engine (PO vs GRN vs Invoice). I implemented a cryptographic SHA-256 idempotency ledger with SQLite WAL, a 3-state self-healing circuit breaker, and an async saga rollback DAG. Under stress testing, the engine clocked 56,179 records/second with p99 latency under 0.02 milliseconds and 0% duplicate leakage, verified across 15 automated test suites.

evaluations.question: How do you prevent circular event loop deadlocks and thread-safety race conditions in concurrent Python microservices?
evaluations.candidate_response: When scaling concurrent services, binding asyncio.Lock() at import time attaches it to whatever loop was active at import, causing deadlocks when called from distinct loops. I implemented lazy property initialization so locks bind only inside active running coroutines. Furthermore, for in-memory telemetry registries accessed across worker threads, I upgraded non-reentrant threading.Lock to threading.RLock, allowing re-entrant inspection without self-deadlock.

evaluations.question: Walk me through how you negotiated with suppliers to drive hard-dollar savings without damaging vendor relationships.
evaluations.candidate_response: Third-party event and staging aggregators routinely mark up fabrication, sound, and lighting quotes by 20-30%. Over 300+ project deployments, I audited our supply chain, bypassed broker middlemen, and established direct relationships with primary fabricators and equipment yards. By offering guaranteed volume multi-deployment commitments and structured milestone payments, I negotiated locked-in rate cards that yielded a recurring 15% net cost reduction with 100% on-time delivery across all operations.
